# Deuteronomy Chapter 12 — SOPHIA Consensus Translation
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **Sources:** EMET (literal), LOGOS (formal), PNEUMA (dynamic) | **Leningrad Codex:** Folios 208–210 | **Vaticanus:** pp. 150–151
**Disagreement Log:** `disagreements/DEU_012.md`

---

## Council Notes

**Chapter Overview:** Deuteronomy 12 opens the Deuteronomic law code (chs. 12–26), establishing the foundational principle of centralized worship. Structure: (1) Destroy Canaanite cult sites (vv. 1–4); (2) The positive command — bring all offerings to the chosen place (vv. 5–7); (3) The contrast with wilderness improvisational practice (vv. 8–12); (4) Warning against offering burnt offerings in unauthorized places (vv. 13–14); (5) The secular slaughter concession — profane meat may be eaten anywhere (vv. 15–16); (6) What must be eaten only at the chosen place (vv. 17–19); (7) The distant community — secular slaughter when the sanctuary is far (vv. 20–25); (8) Handling holy things (vv. 26–27); (9) Summary obedience charge (v. 28); (10) Warning against imitating Canaanite religion (vv. 29–31); (11) Canonical closing formula (v. 32).

**Key Rulings:**
- **V.1 — "statutes and ordinances" vs. "statutes and rules":** EMET/PNEUMA: "statutes and ordinances"; LOGOS: "statutes and rules." Hebrew chuqqim u-mishpatim. Consensus: "statutes and ordinances" — established rendering throughout Deuteronomy.
- **V.1 — "upon the ground" vs. "on the earth" vs. "on earth":** Three translators diverge. Hebrew ha-adamah. Consensus: "on the earth" — standard rendering of ha-adamah in the Deuteronomic formula.
- **V.2 — "surely destroy" vs. "completely demolish":** EMET: "surely destroy"; LOGOS: "surely destroy"; PNEUMA: "completely demolish." Hebrew abed te'abedun (absolute infinitive construction). Consensus: "You shall utterly destroy" — the absolute infinitive demands intensification; "utterly" is the established English rendering.
- **V.2 — "luxuriant tree" vs. "green tree" vs. "spreading tree":** EMET: "luxuriant tree"; LOGOS: "green tree"; PNEUMA: "spreading tree." Hebrew ra'anan = fresh/green/flourishing. Consensus: "leafy tree" — captures the cultic connotation (shade-giving, verdant) without being too interpretive.
- **V.3 — "smash" vs. "dash in pieces":** EMET: "smash their pillars"; LOGOS: "dash in pieces their pillars"; PNEUMA: "smash their sacred pillars." Hebrew shibbar = to shatter/smash. Consensus: "smash their pillars" — direct and accurate; "dash in pieces" is archaic.
- **V.3 — "hew down" vs. "chop down" vs. "hack down":** EMET: "hew down"; LOGOS: "chop down"; PNEUMA: "hack down." Hebrew gidda' = to cut/hew down. Consensus: "cut down" — most neutral and precise.
- **V.3 — "carved images" vs. "carved images" vs. "carved images":** All three agree on "carved images" for pesilei eloheihem.
- **V.4 — "You shall not do so" vs. "You shall not worship...in that way":** EMET: "You shall not do so to the LORD your God"; LOGOS: "You shall not worship the LORD your God in that way"; PNEUMA: "You must not worship the LORD your God in the way they worshipped theirs." Hebrew lo-ta'asun ken = "you shall not do so." Consensus: "You shall not do so to the LORD your God" — EMET's literal rendering is preferred; "worship" is added by LOGOS/PNEUMA and is interpretive.
- **V.5 — "his dwelling" vs. "make his habitation there" vs. "as his dwelling":** The Hebrew leshikhno (for his dwelling/to establish his dwelling) is disputed in v.5. Consensus: "to make his dwelling there" — matches the parallel in v.11 (leshakken shemo sham) and avoids EMET's bracketed gloss.
- **V.6 — "contribution of your hand" vs. "contribution that you present":** EMET: "contribution of your hand"; LOGOS: "contribution that you present"; PNEUMA: "your contributions." Hebrew terumah = contribution/offering. Consensus: "the contribution of your hand" — EMET's literal rendering preserves the gesture-language of the Hebrew; "of your hand" signals a hand-lifted offering.
- **V.7 — "putting-forth of your hand" vs. "all that you undertake":** EMET: "the putting-forth of your hand"; LOGOS: "all that you undertake"; PNEUMA: "everything your hands have worked for." Hebrew mishloach yadkhem = the sending-forth/undertaking of your hand. Consensus: "all that you put your hand to" — natural English idiom that preserves the hand-imagery.
- **V.8 — "every man" vs. "everyone" vs. "everyone":** EMET: "every man [doing] what is right in his own eyes"; LOGOS: "everyone doing whatever is right in his own eyes"; PNEUMA: "everyone doing whatever seems right in their own eyes." Consensus: "each man doing what is right in his own eyes" — "man" (ish) is the Hebrew; maintaining masculine singular preserves the idiom's resonance with Judges 17:6 and 21:25.
- **V.10 — "Yarden" vs. "Jordan":** EMET: "the Yarden"; LOGOS: "the Jordan"; PNEUMA: "the Jordan." Consensus: "the Jordan" — established English name form.
- **V.10 — "dwell in security" vs. "live in safety":** EMET: "dwell in security"; LOGOS: "live in safety"; PNEUMA: "living in safety." Hebrew betach = securely/safely. Consensus: "dwell in safety" — "dwell" (yashab) is more literal; "safety" is slightly more natural than "security."
- **V.11 — "cause his name to dwell there" vs. "make his name dwell there":** EMET: "to cause his name to dwell there [leshakken shemo sham]"; LOGOS: "to make his name dwell there"; PNEUMA: "as a dwelling for his name." Consensus: "to make his name dwell there" — LOGOS's rendering is clean and accurate; EMET's causative ("cause") is technically correct but heavier.
- **V.11 — "choice vow-offerings" vs. "finest vow offerings":** EMET: "choice vow-offerings"; LOGOS: "finest vow offerings"; PNEUMA: "choice vow offerings." Hebrew mivchar = choice/best. Consensus: "your choice vow offerings."
- **V.12 — "within your gates" vs. "within your towns":** EMET: "within your gates"; LOGOS: "within your towns"; PNEUMA: "from your towns." Hebrew bish'arekhem = within your gates. Consensus: "within your gates" — "gates" is the literal Hebrew term; a gate idiomatically means "settlement" but the project preserves the literal image.
- **V.15 — "in all the desire of your soul" vs. "as much as you desire" vs. "wherever you wish":** EMET: "in all the desire of your soul"; LOGOS: "as much as you desire"; PNEUMA: "wherever you wish." Hebrew bekhol-avvat nafshekha = in all the craving of your soul. Consensus: "in all the craving of your soul" — preserves the Hebrew nephesh/craving idiom.
- **V.17 — "new wine" vs. "wine" / "fresh oil" vs. "oil":** EMET: "your new wine and of your fresh oil"; LOGOS: "your wine or of your oil"; PNEUMA: "wine, or olive oil." Hebrew tirosh (new wine) and yitshar (fresh oil/anointing oil). Consensus: "your new wine and your fresh oil" — the specific Hebrew terms tirosh and yitshar are preserved.
- **V.19 — "forsake" vs. "neglect":** EMET: "lest you forsake the Levite"; LOGOS: "that you do not neglect the Levite"; PNEUMA: "not to neglect the Levite." Hebrew azab = to abandon/forsake. Consensus: "lest you forsake the Levite" — azab is a strong word; "forsake" is more precise than "neglect."
- **V.20 — "craves" vs. "crave" phrasing:** EMET: "because your soul craves to eat meat"; LOGOS: "because you crave meat"; PNEUMA: "and you crave meat and say, 'I want to eat meat.'" Consensus: follows EMET/LOGOS phrasing more closely while simplifying PNEUMA's repetition.
- **V.23 — "be strong not to eat" vs. "be sure that you do not eat" vs. "be very firm on this point":** EMET: "Only be strong not to eat the blood"; LOGOS: "Only be sure that you do not eat the blood"; PNEUMA: "But be very firm on this point: do not eat the blood." Hebrew raq chazaq = only be strong. Consensus: "Only be strong not to eat the blood" — EMET preserves the unusual "be strong" (chazaq) idiom; the phrase is striking and should not be smoothed over.
- **V.23 — "the blood — it is the life" vs. "the blood is the life" vs. "the blood is the life":** EMET: "for the blood — it is the life [dam hu ha-nefesh]"; LOGOS: "for the blood is the life"; PNEUMA: "for the blood is the life." Consensus: "for the blood — it is the life" — EMET's dash preserves the Hebrew pronoun equation (dam / hu / ha-nefesh).
- **V.23 — "meat" vs. "flesh":** EMET: "not eat the life together with the meat"; LOGOS: "not eat the life with the flesh"; PNEUMA: "not eat the life with the meat." Hebrew basar = flesh/meat. Consensus: "meat" in the secular context of this passage.
- **V.27 — "the meat and the blood" vs. "the flesh and the blood":** EMET: "the meat and the blood"; LOGOS: "the flesh and the blood"; PNEUMA: "the meat and the blood." Consensus: "the flesh and the blood" — in the sacrificial context (v.27) "flesh" (basar) is more appropriate than "meat."
- **V.27 — "poured out against the altar" vs. "poured out on the altar":** EMET: "poured out against the altar"; LOGOS: "poured out on the altar"; PNEUMA: "poured out beside the altar." Hebrew al-hamizbeach = upon/against the altar. Consensus: "poured out on the altar" — LOGOS is most natural; EMET's "against" is overly literal; PNEUMA's "beside" is too distant.
- **V.28 — "good and the right" vs. "good and right":** EMET: "the good and the right"; LOGOS: "what is good and right"; PNEUMA: "what is good and right." Consensus: "what is good and right" — LOGOS/PNEUMA's phrasing flows more naturally.
- **V.29 — "cuts off" vs. "cuts off before you":** EMET: "cuts off the nations to whom you are going"; LOGOS: "cuts off before you the nations whom you go in to dispossess"; PNEUMA: "has cut off before you the nations." Consensus: follows LOGOS structure.
- **V.30 — "be ensnared after them" vs. "ensnared to follow them" vs. "ensnared into imitating them":** EMET: "lest you be ensnared after them"; LOGOS: "that you be not ensnared to follow them"; PNEUMA: "that you are not ensnared into imitating them." Hebrew pen-tinaqqesh achareihem = lest you be snared after them. Consensus: "lest you be ensnared following after them" — preserves "after them" (achareihem) which is literal and significant.
- **V.31 — "abomination [to'evah]" vs. "abominable thing" vs. "detestable":** EMET: "every abomination [to'evah]"; LOGOS: "every abominable thing"; PNEUMA: "everything...is detestable." Hebrew to'evah = abomination. Consensus: "every abomination" — EMET's rendering is the established English term; the bracketed gloss is removed from the text.
- **V.32 — "Every word" vs. "Everything":** EMET: "Every word which I am commanding you"; LOGOS: "Everything that I command you"; PNEUMA: "Everything I am commanding you." Hebrew kol-hadavar = every word/thing. Consensus: "Every word that I am commanding you" — preserves "word" (davar) literally; the closing formula invokes the integrity of the spoken covenant word.
- **V.32 — "add upon it" vs. "add to it":** EMET: "you shall not add upon it"; LOGOS: "You shall not add to it"; PNEUMA: "Do not add to it." Consensus: "you shall not add to it" — LOGOS's phrasing is most natural.

---

## Consensus Translation — Deuteronomy 12

**1** These are the statutes and the ordinances that you shall be careful to do in the land that the LORD, the God of your fathers, has given you to possess — all the days that you live on the earth.

**2** You shall utterly destroy all the places where the nations whom you are dispossessing served their gods — on the high mountains and on the hills and under every leafy tree.

**3** And you shall tear down their altars and smash their pillars and burn their Asherah poles with fire, and the carved images of their gods you shall cut down, and you shall destroy their name from that place.

**4** You shall not do so to the LORD your God.

**5** But only to the place that the LORD your God will choose from all your tribes to put his name — to make his dwelling there — there you shall seek, and there you shall come.

**6** And there you shall bring your burnt offerings and your sacrifices, your tithes and the contribution of your hand, your vow offerings and your freewill offerings, and the firstborn of your herd and of your flock.

**7** And there you shall eat before the LORD your God, and you shall rejoice in all that you put your hand to — you and your households — in which the LORD your God has blessed you.

**8** You shall not do according to all that we are doing here today — each man doing what is right in his own eyes —

**9** for you have not yet come to the rest and to the inheritance that the LORD your God is giving you.

**10** But when you cross over the Jordan and dwell in the land that the LORD your God is giving you as inheritance, and he gives you rest from all your enemies surrounding you so that you dwell in safety —

**11** then to the place that the LORD your God will choose to make his name dwell there, there you shall bring all that I am commanding you: your burnt offerings and your sacrifices, your tithes and the contribution of your hand, and all your choice vow offerings that you vow to the LORD.

**12** And you shall rejoice before the LORD your God — you and your sons and your daughters and your male servants and your female servants and the Levite who is within your gates, for he has no portion or inheritance with you.

**13** Take care lest you offer your burnt offerings in every place that you see.

**14** But only in the place that the LORD will choose in one of your tribes — there you shall offer your burnt offerings, and there you shall do all that I am commanding you.

**15** However, in all the craving of your soul you may slaughter and eat meat according to the blessing of the LORD your God that he gives to you in all your gates; the unclean and the clean may eat of it alike, as of the gazelle and as of the deer.

**16** Only the blood you shall not eat; on the ground you shall pour it out like water.

**17** You are not able to eat within your gates the tithe of your grain and of your new wine and of your fresh oil, or the firstborn of your herd and of your flock, or any of your vow offerings that you vow, or your freewill offerings, or the contribution of your hand.

**18** But before the LORD your God you shall eat them — in the place that the LORD your God will choose — you and your son and your daughter and your male servant and your female servant and the Levite who is within your gates; and you shall rejoice before the LORD your God in all that you put your hand to.

**19** Take care lest you forsake the Levite all your days on your ground.

**20** When the LORD your God enlarges your territory as he has spoken to you, and you say, "I will eat meat" — because your soul craves to eat meat — in all the craving of your soul you may eat meat.

**21** If the place that the LORD your God will choose to put his name is too far from you, then you may slaughter from your herd and from your flock that the LORD has given you, as I commanded you, and you shall eat within your gates in all the craving of your soul.

**22** However, as the gazelle and the deer are eaten, so you shall eat it; the unclean and the clean alike may eat of it.

**23** Only be strong not to eat the blood, for the blood — it is the life; and you shall not eat the life together with the meat.

**24** You shall not eat it; on the ground you shall pour it out like water.

**25** You shall not eat it, so that it may go well with you and with your sons after you, when you do what is right in the eyes of the LORD.

**26** Only your holy things that you have and your vow offerings you shall take up and come to the place that the LORD will choose.

**27** And you shall offer your burnt offerings — the flesh and the blood — on the altar of the LORD your God; and the blood of your sacrifices shall be poured out on the altar of the LORD your God, and the flesh you shall eat.

**28** Keep and hear all these words that I am commanding you, so that it may go well with you and with your sons after you forever, when you do what is good and right in the eyes of the LORD your God.

**29** When the LORD your God cuts off before you the nations to whom you are going in to dispossess them, and you dispossess them and dwell in their land,

**30** take care lest you be ensnared following after them after their being destroyed from before you, and lest you inquire after their gods, saying, "How did these nations serve their gods? And I also will do thus."

**31** You shall not do so to the LORD your God, for every abomination that the LORD hates they did for their gods — for also their sons and their daughters they burned in the fire to their gods.

**32** Every word that I am commanding you — it you shall be careful to do; you shall not add to it and you shall not diminish from it.

---

## Verse-by-Verse Ruling Notes

**V.1:** "Statutes and ordinances" — chuqqim u-mishpatim, established Deuteronomic pair. LOGOS's "rules" for mishpatim is less precise; "ordinances" (legal judgments) is the project standard. "On the earth" for ha-adamah; the ground is the physical Promised Land.

**V.2:** "Utterly destroy" renders the absolute infinitive abed te'abedun — a doubling construction requiring intensification. All three translators render something comparable; "utterly" is the strongest and most established English equivalent. "Leafy tree" for etz ra'anan — EMET's "luxuriant" and PNEUMA's "spreading" are both defensible; "leafy" captures the visual sense of a shady cultic site.

**V.3:** PNEUMA adds "sacred" to "sacred pillars" — not in the Hebrew (matsevot). Removed. EMET's "tear down" and "smash" are preferred over LOGOS's "dash in pieces." "Cut down" for gidda' follows the dominant sense of the root.

**V.4:** LOGOS and PNEUMA both render "worship" — but the Hebrew lo-ta'asun ken (you shall not do so) does not specify worship; it contrasts the destruction of Canaanite sites with what Israel shall not do to the LORD's worship. The bare "do so" is more precise and theologically sharper: destroying YHWH's altar is the implicit warning.

**V.5:** The Deuteronomic centralization formula appears here in its full form. "To make his dwelling there" renders leshikhno (Ketiv/Qere variants): the Qere reads leshakken shemo (to cause his name to dwell) but the Ketiv (as read in this verse) is leshikhno (for his dwelling). Consensus preserves the ambiguity by choosing "to make his dwelling" — encompassing both the Name theology reading and the Presence reading. The formula "there you shall seek, and there you shall come" preserves EMET's literal pair.

**V.6:** "The contribution of your hand" — terumah yedkhem preserves the hand-imagery that LOGOS dissolves into "contribution that you present." The offering is physically hand-raised.

**V.7:** "All that you put your hand to" — a natural English idiom rendering mishloach yadkhem. EMET's "putting-forth of your hand" is accurate but wooden. LOGOS's "undertake" loses the hand-imagery.

**V.8:** "Each man doing what is right in his own eyes" — ish/kol-hayashar be'einav. The masculine singular ish is preserved, keeping resonance with the Judges refrain. PNEUMA's "their own eyes" (plural) smooths over the Hebrew.

**V.10:** "Cross over the Jordan" — EMET's transliteration "Yarden" replaced by established English form "Jordan." "Dwell in safety" — betach has the sense of secure, unafraid dwelling; both LOGOS and PNEUMA use "safety" which is preferred over EMET's "security."

**V.11:** "Make his name dwell there" — the leshakken shemo sham formula is the purest expression of Deuteronomic Name theology. "Your choice vow offerings" — mivchar nidreikhem, EMET and PNEUMA's "choice" is exact; LOGOS's "finest" is also accurate.

**V.12:** "Within your gates" — bish'arekhem. LOGOS and PNEUMA both modernize to "within your towns." The project has consistently preserved "gates" as the Deuteronomic idiom for settlement/community (cf. DEU_010, DEU_011). Maintained.

**V.13:** "Take care lest" — hishamer lekha (EMET's "Be careful lest") vs. LOGOS's "Take care that you do not." Consensus: "Take care lest" — slightly more formal, matching the chapter's legislative register.

**V.15:** "In all the craving of your soul" — bekhol-avvat nafshekha. LOGOS's "as much as you desire" loses the nefesh-craving language that echoes through vv. 15, 20, 21. PNEUMA's "wherever you wish" misdirects (the freedom is about quantity and location, not just location). EMET's literal rendering is preserved. Note the gazelle-deer comparison: these wild animals cannot be sacrificed; they model the category of food that does not require sanctuary contact.

**V.16:** "On the ground" — EMET's "upon the ground" and LOGOS's "on the earth" both work; "on the ground" is most natural and fits the physical action described.

**V.17:** "New wine" (tirosh) and "fresh oil" (yitshar) — the specific Hebrew terms are preserved. LOGOS flattens to "wine" and "oil," losing the distinction between tirosh (unfermented grape juice / new wine) and yayin (fermented wine).

**V.19:** "Lest you forsake the Levite" — azab = to abandon/forsake. LOGOS and PNEUMA use "neglect," which softens the force of azab. The Levite's vulnerability demands the stronger word.

**V.20:** The verse's repetition of "craving" (avvah/craving, v.20: vekhi te'avveh nafshekha) mirrors v.15. The structure "I will eat meat — because your soul craves to eat meat" preserves the quoted speech and explanatory clause as in the Hebrew.

**V.23:** "Be strong not to eat the blood" — raq chazaq = only be strong/only be resolute. This is an unusual command: strength language applied to dietary restraint. All three translators soften it; EMET alone preserves "be strong." The Hebrew deserves to keep this unusual idiom. "The blood — it is the life" — the dash-equation (EMET) is maintained for dam / hu / ha-nefesh.

**V.26:** "Holy things" — qodashekha = your holy/sacred things. All three agree on the concept. PNEUMA's "things you have vowed to give" is interpretive. EMET and LOGOS more literal.

**V.27:** "The flesh and the blood" — in the sacrificial context "flesh" (basar) is more appropriate than "meat." The blood poured on the altar vs. the flesh eaten by the worshiper is a distinction that runs through Leviticus and Numbers; "flesh" maintains the ritual register.

**V.28:** "Keep and hear" — shemor veshama'ta. EMET preserves the pair literally. LOGOS's "Be careful to obey" collapses both verbs. The two-verb structure (heed and listen) is a Deuteronomic feature worth preserving.

**V.29:** LOGOS places "before you" (mippanekha) accurately in the sentence. EMET's positioning is also correct but less idiomatic.

**V.30:** "Ensnared following after them" — tinaqqesh achareihem. "After them" (achareihem) is retained because it is theologically loaded: the snare is not merely imitation but following behind/after — the image of becoming a devotee walking in their train. PNEUMA's "imitating" drops this spatial-directional language.

**V.31:** "Every abomination that the LORD hates" — kol to'evat YHWH asher sane. EMET's bracketed [to'evah] in the translation text is removed; "abomination" is the established English rendering. PNEUMA's "detestable to the LORD — things he hates" doubles up explanatorily; the Hebrew is a single relative clause.

**V.32:** "Every word" — kol-hadavar. The chapter closes with davar (word), not simply "thing." "Every word I am commanding you" emphasizes that the covenant is a verbal/spoken deposit — grounding the add/diminish prohibition in the word's completeness. "You shall not add to it and you shall not diminish from it" — the two negative jussives are preserved in parallel.

---

## Textual Notes

**V.2 — Canaanite cultic landscape:** The description "high mountains and hills and under every leafy tree" is a fixed topographic formula for Canaanite open-air shrines (cf. Jer. 2:20; Ezek. 6:13; Hos. 4:13). The LXX (Vat. pp.150–151) renders ὑπὸ πᾶν ξύλον δασύ (under every thick/leafy tree), confirming ra'anan as thick/leafy.

**V.3 — Asherah poles and pillars:** The masseboth (standing stones, pillars) were stone steles; the asherot (Asherah poles) were wooden cult objects associated with the goddess Asherah. Both are to be physically destroyed, not merely abandoned. The LXX renders τὰ ἄλση αὐτῶν (their sacred groves) for asherot and τὰς στήλας αὐτῶν (their steles/pillars) for masseboth.

**V.5 — The centralization formula:** The phrase "the place that the LORD your God will choose" (hamaqom asher-yivchar YHWH eloheikhem) appears seven times in this chapter (vv.5, 11, 14, 18, 21, 26 — and implicitly in v.13). This is the theological axis of the entire Deuteronomic law code. The place is unnamed in Moses' address; Jerusalem is not yet identified. The LXX renders ὃν ἂν ἐκλέξηται Κύριος ὁ θεός σου (whichever the LORD your God shall choose) consistently.

**V.5 — Name theology:** leshakken shemo sham (v.11) — "to make his name dwell there." The verb shakan (to dwell, tabernacle) grounds the Shekhinah concept. Deuteronomy's distinctive contribution is that it is the divine Name (shem), not the Glory-cloud (kavod), that dwells at the sanctuary. This preserves divine transcendence while affirming real presence. The LXX renders ἐπικληθῆναι τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ ἐκεῖ (for his name to be called/invoked there) — a slightly different nuance (invocation vs. indwelling).

**V.8 — "What is right in his own eyes":** Hebrew כָּל-הַיָּשָׁר בְּעֵינָיו — the refrain of Judges 17:6 and 21:25. Here the phrase is not yet a condemnation of moral anarchy but a description of the unavoidably decentralized worship of the wilderness period, which the central sanctuary will supersede.

**V.15 — Secular slaughter:** This passage introduces the category of hullin (profane/secular) slaughter. In contrast to Lev. 17:3–4, which required all slaughter at the tent of meeting, Deuteronomy permits non-sacrificial slaughter anywhere, once the community is settled and the sanctuary is established. The gazelle and deer model the category — they cannot be sacrificed (wild animals), so their consumption has always been "secular." Ritual purity distinctions do not apply to this category of food.

**V.23 — Blood prohibition:** dam hu ha-nefesh — "the blood, it is the life." The equation of blood with nefesh (life-force) is the theological foundation of the blood prohibition throughout the Torah (Gen. 9:4; Lev. 17:11, 14; Deut. 12:23). To eat blood is to consume the life that belongs to God alone. The LXX renders ὅτι τὸ αἷμα αὐτοῦ ψυχή ἐστιν (for its blood is the soul/life).

**V.31 — Child sacrifice:** הַגַּם אֶת-בְּנֵיהֶם וְאֶת-בְּנֹתֵיהֶם יִשְׂרְפוּ בָאֵשׁ לֵאלֹהֵיהֶם — "for also their sons and daughters they burned in the fire to their gods." This is identified with Molech worship (cf. Lev. 18:21; 2 Kgs 23:10). The LXX confirms: καὶ γὰρ τοὺς υἱοὺς αὐτῶν καὶ τὰς θυγατέρας αὐτῶν κατακαίουσιν ἐν πυρὶ τοῖς θεοῖς αὐτῶν. The gam (also/even) expresses rhetorical escalation — this is the ultimate marker of to'evah.

**V.32 — Canonical closing formula:** לֹא תֹסֵף עָלָיו וְלֹא תִגְרַע מִמֶּנּוּ — "you shall not add to it and you shall not diminish from it." This formula appears also in Deut. 4:2 and is echoed in Rev. 22:18–19. It marks the concluded, inviolable character of the instruction. The LXX renders οὐ προσθήσεις ἐπ᾽ αὐτό, οὐδὲ ἀφελεῖς ἀπ᾽ αὐτοῦ (you shall not add to it, nor remove from it).

---

— SOPHIA
